clue.text: Some may be inclined to get you down

definitions.text: Some may be inclined to get you down

parts.words: Some may be inclined to get you down
parts.note: reads like people disposed to depress you, but describes inclined ground that carries a skier or walker downhill

explanation.surface: A warning about gloomy people who tend to drag your spirits low.
explanation.definitionFit: Slopes are inclined stretches of ground, and going down them takes you to the bottom.

clue.text: Fire-place, perhaps, in an old castle

definitions.text: Fire-place, perhaps, in an old castle

parts.words: Fire-place, perhaps, in an old castle
parts.note: suggests a hearth, but read as a place to fire from: a slit in a castle wall for shooting arrows

explanation.surface: A hearth found in the hall of a medieval castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Castle walls had narrow slits through which archers fired, a place for firing in another sense.

clue.text: The waiting game?

parts.note: a card game played alone, whose name is also the virtue needed for waiting

explanation.surface: A strategy of holding back and biding one's time.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire card play is known in Britain by the name of the virtue of enduring delay calmly.

clue.text: No lengthy Terpsichorean display

parts.note: Terpsichore is the Muse of dance; no lengthy hints at a mere footfall, a short pace, naming a kind of dance

explanation.surface: A brief dance routine rather than a long ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance performed with intricate footwork; a single footfall is only a short distance, hence no lengthy.

clue.text: Device no elephant needs

parts.note: an elephant is proverbially said never to forget, so it would have no use for a memory aid

explanation.surface: A gadget that an elephant could happily do without.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory aid, such as a rhyme for remembering facts, is a device for those who might forget.

clue.text: Arrest of young girl, say, for taking thinks wrongly

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: apprehension is arrest, and miss is a young girl, so arresting a miss is miss apprehension

explanation.surface: A police report on detaining a girl for wrongful thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'Miss apprehension' (the arrest of a young girl) sounds like the answer. 'thinks' is as printed, where 'things' is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistaken understanding is a taking of matters the wrong way.

clue.text: Like the scene of Oberon's meeting with Titania

definitions.text: Like the scene of Oberon's meeting with Titania

parts.words: Like the scene of Oberon's meeting with Titania
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Oberon greets Titania with 'Ill met by moonlight', so the scene is lit by the night sky

explanation.surface: A theatre note about the setting of a Shakespearean encounter between fairy king and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy rulers meet at night under the light of the moon in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: A devilish calling?

parts.note: calling suggests a vocation, but means a name; Old Nick is a name for the Devil

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone's profession is wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal name given to someone; Nick is a nickname for Satan, hence devilish.

clue.text: Street of Islam

definitions.meaning: a curved row of houses or road
the symbol associated with the Islamic faith

explanation.surface: Naming a road in a Muslim district.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved terrace of houses is one sense; the waxing moon shape is the emblem of the Muslim world.

clue.text: There's no advantage in going barefoot

definitions.meaning: an old word for useless or unprofitable, since boot once meant profit

explanation.surface: A remark that walking without shoes gains you nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot' in old English meant profit or advantage ('to boot' survives), so the word also means useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking profit makes something futile, and lacking footwear leaves the feet bare; both senses share one word.

clue.text: This is delivered by jet

parts.note: suggests something sent by jet aircraft, but means a spray of water squirted from a nozzle

explanation.surface: Something that arrives by jet aeroplane, like airmail.
explanation.definitionFit: A douche is a stream of water directed at the body, which comes out of a nozzle as a jet.

clue.text: Ticks off members of the flock who visit it?

definitions.text: Ticks off members of the flock who visit it?

parts.words: Ticks off members of the flock who visit it?
parts.note: ticks off sounds like a rebuke to churchgoers, but means removing parasites from sheep that are plunged into it

explanation.surface: A vicar scolding members of the congregation who come to see him.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath of insecticide into which sheep are plunged rids them of ticks and other parasites.

clue.text: Better to leave this instruction group?

definitions.meaning: patients leave a medical centre better, that is, recovered
a session where a group is given expert teaching, as in a golf one

explanation.surface: Asking whether it would be wiser to quit a training class.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical centre is where the sick are treated and leave healthier; a teaching session for a group of learners shares the name.

clue.text: Players internally torn with differences such a this

indicators.note: the players are said to hold something inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play

indicators.note: the letters of torn are given with differences, that is altered in order

explanation.surface: Actors inwardly divided because of disagreements among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder; 'with differences' is what reorders it, and 'internally' places it within the players. 'such a this' is printed so (meant 'such as this'), pointing back at the clue's own idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking difference between two things is the very kind of opposition the clue describes.

clue.text: It smoothes the beach daily

parts.note: sand is what a beach is made of
a daily is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: Something that levels the seashore every day, like the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive paper is rubbed on wood to make it smooth.

clue.text: Subjunctively he is no male divinity

parts.note: taken as written
in the subjunctive mood, is becomes be, as in 'if he be'

explanation.surface: A grammatical point that he, in the subjunctive, is not a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subjunctively' tells you to put 'he is' into the old subjunctive form, 'he be'. Hebe is the Greek goddess of youth, cupbearer to the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was a Greek goddess, so a female deity rather than a male one.

clue.text: She turns, for a change, to the chase

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman who switches to hunting as a new pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges SHE TURNS; the whole clue also describes the answer, a woman who takes to the chase.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who hunts game is one devoted to the chase, as Diana was.

clue.text: Common mouse is not 'the white variety

definitions.text: Common mouse is not 'the white variety

parts.words: Common mouse is not 'the white variety
parts.note: suggests a house mouse rather than a white lab mouse, but mouse is slang for a bruised eye after a punch

explanation.surface: A note that the ordinary house mouse is not the white kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruised, darkened eye from a blow is called a mouse in slang, and it is dark rather than white.

clue.text: The French infiltration would make this party select

indicators.note: the clue says the French article getting into the answer would turn it into select, so take it back out of select

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A French presence would make a political party more exclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: Work backwards: SELECT with LE removed leaves SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a faction or breakaway group, a party in the sense of a body of adherents.

clue.text: I got on after row with a servant

indicators.note: the pieces I and on are placed after the rowing word

parts.note: to scull is to row with oars
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone getting along well with a servant after an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is rowing a boat. A scullion was a kitchen servant doing menial work.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a lowly kitchen hand who washed dishes and pots.

clue.text: Her name is on a relic, oddly enough

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are put in an odd, unexpected order

explanation.surface: A woman's name inscribed on an ancient artefact, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Caroline is a girl's given name.

clue.text: He should make things go

parts.note: sounds like a motivator or organiser, but means one who gets engines and machines running

explanation.surface: A description of a go-getting manager who drives a project.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic repairs engines and machinery so that they work.

clue.text: One shouldn't get it in an easy-chair

definitions.text: One shouldn't get it in an easy-chair

parts.words: One shouldn't get it in an easy-chair
parts.note: French mal plus aise is literally ill-ease, which no one should feel in a chair designed for comfort

explanation.surface: Advice that a comfortable armchair should not make you feel uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a vague feeling of unease or illness, the opposite of comfort.

clue.text: Bring down the gear

definitions.meaning: as in rugby or football, stopping an opponent by grabbing them to the ground

explanation.surface: An order to lower the equipment from a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounding an opponent in rugby is one sense; fishing equipment such as rods and lines is another.

clue.text: Great little man in short to make game of

definitions.meaning: the French emperor, famously short in stature yet a great figure
a card game, shortened to nap

explanation.surface: Someone small but great being made fun of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' hints at the emperor's height and at the card game being known in short form as nap; 'to make game of' disguises the game as mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte was a celebrated French emperor of small stature; a trick-taking card game also bears his name.

clue.text: You can see when it's raised

definitions.text: You can see when it's raised

parts.words: You can see when it's raised
parts.note: sounds like something visible when lifted, but means a flap of skin over the eye that lets you see when it is up

explanation.surface: Something that becomes visible once it is hoisted, like a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: When the skin flap over the eye is lifted, the eye is open and vision is possible.

clue.text: Zulu warriors surround the boundary first of all

indicators.note: the warriors close in on all sides of the boundary, so it sits inside them

parts.note: impis are Zulu regiments of warriors
a rim is an edge or boundary

explanation.surface: An account of Zulu fighters encircling a frontier before anything else happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprimis is a Latin adverb used in lists meaning in the first place.

clue.text: No trace of one in Mother Hubbard's cupboard

definitions.text: No trace of one in Mother Hubbard's cupboard

parts.words: No trace of one in Mother Hubbard's cupboard
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme cupboard was bare, with not even a bone, so no bony frame could hide there, unlike the proverbial family secret in the cupboard

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme cupboard so bare there was nothing at all inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Mother Hubbard is the nursery-rhyme woman whose cupboard was bare, so her dog got no bone; the idiom is a family secret kept in the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A bony frame is the proverbial secret hidden in a cupboard, and it is made entirely of bone.

clue.text: Smuggler in a hurry

definitions.meaning: one who carries contraband, as in gun or rum dealing

explanation.surface: A contraband carrier rushing to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum or gun carrier is a smuggler; someone sprinting is also one on the move fast.
